abertura: In the lesson you are going to read two reviews of the same film. One says yes, the other says no.
Three of the sentences below are true. Mark those three.

itens.t: A review says what someone thinks about something.
itens.porque: That is the opinion, and it is the easiest part to write. It is also the part nobody can argue with.

itens.t: A review has to tell the whole story.
itens.porque: A review that tells the whole story is a spoiler. Reviews say enough for you to decide, and no more.

itens.t: A good review explains why.
itens.porque: The reason is the only part the reader can actually use. Without it, a review is just a number of stars.

itens.t: You have to agree with a review for it to be useful.
itens.porque: You can read a bad review, see the reason, and decide that the reason does not bother you. That review just helped you.

itens.t: A review usually ends by telling you what to do.
itens.porque: Watch it, skip it, wait for season two. That is the recommendation, and it is what the reader came for.

itens.t: Reviews are always written by professionals.
itens.porque: Most of the reviews you read were written by people your age, on a phone, right after watching.

sec1.rationale: Opinion, reason, recommendation. Three different jobs, and the middle one is the one people remember.

nota.texto: For seventeen lessons you asked for things in English: a table, a ticket, directions. Nobody once asked you what you thought. This one does — about something you choose.

sec1.pt: Na aula você vai ler duas resenhas do mesmo filme: uma recomenda e a outra não. Antes disso, marque as três frases verdadeiras sobre para que serve uma resenha.

abertura: Choose the meaning that fits the way the word is used in a review.

itens.t: worth watching
alts: good enough to spend the time on
itens.ok: good enough to spend the time on

itens.t: to guess
alts: to know it before it is shown
to watch it a second time
itens.ok: to know it before it is shown

itens.t: slow
alts: it takes a long time to happen
itens.ok: it takes a long time to happen

itens.t: the ending
alts: the last part of the story
the best part of the story
itens.ok: the last part of the story

itens.t: the acting
alts: the way the actors play the people
itens.ok: the way the actors play the people

itens.t: lazy

nota.titulo: Six words you will read tomorrow
nota.texto: All six are in the two reviews you are going to read. Lazy writing is the one people use most and expect least: it is not about the writer being tired — it is about the easy choice being made instead of the good one.

sec2.pt: Seis palavras que aparecem nas duas resenhas. Para cada uma, escolha o sentido que ela tem dentro de uma resenha — que nem sempre é o sentido mais comum da palavra.

doc.texto: The first ten minutes are perfect. Then the episode turns into a long conversation in a car, and it never leaves. The acting is great and the writing is lazy. I will watch the next one, but I am not excited about it.

abertura: Every line of a review is one of two things. Which one is each?

itens.t: The first ten minutes are perfect.
itens.porque: Perfect is a judgment. Someone else can watch the same ten minutes and disagree with you.

itens.t: The episode turns into a long conversation in a car.
itens.porque: It happens or it does not, and you can check it by watching. Nothing to agree with.

itens.t: The acting is great.
itens.porque: Great is a judgment too — and this is the line that says why the review still gives three stars.

itens.t: The writing is lazy.
itens.porque: This one sounds like a description, and it is not. It is the writer's judgment about someone else's work.

itens.t: This is the first episode of season two.
itens.porque: It is written at the top of the review, and you can check it. Reading that line is part of reading the review.

itens.t: I am not excited about it.
itens.porque: How someone feels is theirs. It is the shortest opinion in the review, and the one that decides the three stars.

nota.titulo: The line that carries the review
nota.texto: Take the facts out and the review still works. Take the opinions out and there is nothing left. But a review that is only opinion convinces nobody — which is exactly what the next activity is about.

sec3.pt: Leia a resenha do episódio e diga o que é cada linha: uma opinião (o que a pessoa acha, e alguém pode discordar) ou um fato (dá para conferir assistindo).

doc.texto: The first ten minutes are perfect. Then the episode turns into a long conversation in a car, and it never leaves. The acting is great and the writing is lazy. I will watch the next one, but I am not excited about it.

abertura: Three of these are true. Mark those three.

itens.t: The writer likes the beginning of the episode.
itens.porque: “The first ten minutes are perfect.” The praise is there, and it is only for the beginning.

itens.t: The writer thinks the actors do a bad job.
itens.porque: The opposite: “the acting is great”. The complaint is about the writing, and the two are not the same thing.

itens.t: The writer will keep watching the series.
itens.porque: “I will watch the next one” — with “I am not excited about it” right after. Both are true at once, and that is why it is three stars and not one.

itens.t: Most of the episode happens in a car.
itens.porque: “turns into a long conversation in a car, and it never leaves”. Never leaves is the part that tells you it is most of the episode.

itens.t: The writer says the story is easy to guess.
itens.porque: That complaint is not here. This review complains about a long scene, which is a different problem from a predictable story.

itens.t: The writer gave the episode five stars.
itens.porque: Three. The number is at the top, and it is part of the review — a reader checks it before reading a single word.

sec4.rationale: The one that catches people is the sentence about the writer carrying on with the series: the writer will keep watching AND is not excited. Reviews are full of two true things at once, and that is what makes them worth reading.

nota.texto: A review is rarely all yes or all no. This one praises the acting and attacks the writing in the same sentence — and that is what makes the reader believe it.

sec4.pt: A mesma resenha do exercício anterior. Agora leia para achar informação: três das frases são verdadeiras. Marque as três.

abertura: Choose the ending that belongs there. These are the five sentences you will use in the lesson.

What I like
The problem
alts: is that it is too slow
itens.ok: is that it is too slow

itens.t: I would not recommend it,
alts: because of you can guess the ending
for you can guess the ending
because you can guess the ending
itens.ok: because you can guess the ending

itens.t: It is slow,
alts: and that is not the point

nota.titulo: Five sentences, and the reason is inside four of them
nota.texto: Look at where the reason sits in each one: after because, after is that, after but. You never have to wait for someone to ask why — the sentence already has room for it.

sec5.pt: Cada frase começa de um jeito. Escolha o final que combina com o começo. São as cinco frases que você vai dizer em voz alta na aula.

abertura: Write them about something you have really watched. You will say them out loud in the lesson.

itens.t: I think this one is worth {watching|100px}, and I have two reasons.
The first one {is|60px} that the acting is really good.
The other {thing|90px} is that the ending is not what you expect.
I would not recommend it, {because|100px} you can guess the whole story.

nota.titulo: This is your text for the lesson
nota.texto: Four short sentences. In the lesson you will say them without the screen, about something you chose — and then say them again to someone who did not like it.

sec6.pt: Complete as quatro frases sobre alguma coisa que você assistiu de verdade. Na aula você vai dizer essas frases sem a tela.

itens.t: The two main characters feel like real people.
itens.porque: It is her strongest reason, and it is the one that answers “nothing explodes”.

itens.t: You can guess the story in ten minutes.
itens.porque: His main complaint, and the reason two hours feels long to him.

itens.t: The ending stays with you for days.
itens.porque: Both of them talk about the ending. She says it lasts; he says it arrives too late.

itens.t: Two hours is a long time for this story.
itens.porque: Notice that it is not “two hours is too long”. It is long for this story — the length is only a problem because of the plot.

itens.t: It is slow, and that is the point.
itens.porque: She admits the film is slow and turns it into a reason to watch. Chris would call the same thing a defect.

itens.t: The photography is beautiful.
itens.porque: The one that surprises people. The negative review still praises something — and that is what makes the rest of it believable.

ev19.rationale: Five of the six are easy. The last one is the lesson: Chris does not hate everything, and a review that only says “bad” convinces nobody.

itens.t: Both reviews talk about the ending.
itens.porque: Maya: it stays with you. Chris: it is the only surprise and it comes too late. Same part of the film, opposite verdicts.

itens.t: Chris finds something good in the film.
itens.porque: “The photography is beautiful.” He gives it away in the middle of a two-star review.

itens.t: Maya thinks the film is too slow.
itens.porque: She says it is slow, and that this is the point. Slow is her reason to watch it, not her complaint.

itens.t: Chris thinks the story is easy to guess.
itens.porque: “a story you can guess in ten minutes”. It is the reason under every other thing he says.

itens.t: Maya recommends the film because of the photography.
itens.porque: She never mentions the photography. That is Chris. Two reviews of the same film do not have to talk about the same things.

itens.t: Both reviewers watched the film at the cinema.
itens.porque: Neither says where. This is the one that is not in the text at all — and the easiest kind of mistake to make when you are reading fast.

itens.t: It is slow, and that is the point.
itens.porque: It says how she feels about the pace. It does not explain anything and it does not tell you what to do.

itens.t: The two main characters feel like real people.
itens.porque: This is the part you can use. If you like films with real characters, you now know something.

itens.t: Worth watching.
itens.porque: Two words, and it is what the reader came for: do it or do not.

itens.t: Two hours is a long time for a story you can guess in ten minutes.
itens.porque: It explains the verdict instead of repeating it. Notice it is one sentence with two ideas inside.

itens.t: I do not agree.
itens.porque: Pure position, and nothing else. On its own it changes nobody's mind — which is why the next sentence exists.

itens.t: I would not recommend it.
itens.porque: The verdict, said as an instruction. Chris puts his at the end; Maya puts hers at the end too. That is where it usually goes.

gd19.rationale: Opinion, reason, recommendation. Say only the first and you sound like you did not think; say only the third and nobody believes you.

abertura: The three jobs, and what each one sounds like.

tabela: It is worth watching. · I do not agree.
… because the characters feel real. · The problem is that you can guess it.

callout.texto: You read two reviews that disagree, worked out what each person was actually arguing, and then recommended something of your own with two reasons and nothing on the screen. Nobody had asked you what you thought in English before.

What you are trying to do: answer in about a minute, with a recommendation and two different reasons, without writing it first.

A situação: uma amiga pergunta o que assistir hoje à noite. Responda em cerca de um minuto, com uma recomendação e duas razões diferentes, sem escrever antes.

abertura: Write a four-sentence review of something you finished this week.

callout.titulo: Four sentences is the whole thing
callout.texto:
One for what it is, one for what you think, one for the reason, one for what the reader should do.

Try the hard version: put one good thing into a review of something you did not like, the way Chris does. Maya never has to — she liked the film. It is the sentence that makes people believe the rest.

writemore.pt:
Escreva uma resenha de quatro frases sobre alguma coisa que você terminou esta semana: o que é, o que você acha, o motivo, e o que a pessoa deve fazer.

A versão difícil: ponha uma coisa boa numa resenha de algo que você não gostou, como o Chris faz. É a frase que faz o resto ser levado a sério.
